messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: RSF diagnostic plots
parts:
Dear community,

I've just pushed an update to GitHub containing the new and documented intensity() function, see help("intensity"), which plots the log of the intensity (or selection) function with respect to a covariate. For the following plots, I'm using a lowland tapir that selects for the tree-cover variable 'tree'.
In the first plot, only the (black) empirical curve is shown, as no model is provided for the tree-cover dependence. If there are other variables included in the provided model, then they will be accounted for in the calculation of this curve, so that only the dependence on the variable of interest is estimated. Here the model looks approximately quadratic.
In the second plot we included a linear model (red). The red line is the theoretical curve of the fitted RSF model with its estimated uncertainty. Ideally, we want the empirical and theoretical curves to match (within uncertainty).
In the third plot we included a quadratic model.
In the fourth and final plot we included a cubic model.

Finally, model selection yields consistent results with either AICc or BIC:

> summary(RSFS,IC="AICc") ΔAICc ΔRMSPE (m) DOF[area] quadratic 0.0000000 54.83153 9.368759 linear 0.4363133 0.00000 11.773998 cubic 3.8859959 71.20549 8.922395 null 9.1006526 35.60037 12.386550
> summary(RSFS,IC="BIC") ΔBIC ΔRMSPE (m) DOF[area] quadratic 0.000000 54.83153 9.368759 linear 1.357883 0.00000 11.773998 cubic 2.093670 71.20549 8.922395 null 9.735750 35.60037 12.386550

The RSF AICc formula is also improved in this update.

Best,
Chris
